It is a critical factor in determining how quickly data can be accessed and processed by the CPU. A higher memory bandwidth means the CPU can fetch more data at once, which improves performance. For example, if a CPU has a memory bandwidth of 1000 MB/s, it can read and write 1000 MB of data per second, which is significantly faster than a slower bandwidth. This is especially important in applications that require frequent data access, such as scientific simulations or real-time data
